generated_by: Round 18 lane L2 — THE FILTER AS A LEAK
read_this_first: Read each entry's coverage / not_covered fields, not its status (AGENTS.md section 7).

entries.hypothesis: The anti-repeat rule is enforced on the CIPHERTEXT, not on the keystream and not on the plaintext. Seven loci were formalised and simulated: no filter (M0), ciphertext key-skip (M1, the repo's pinned model), ciphertext value-rewrite with the key staying aligned (M2), ciphertext deterministic nudge (M2n), keystream-filtered at generation (M3), plaintext-filtered before encipherment (M4), hard ciphertext rule (M5).
entries.threshold: A model may be called EXCLUDED only if the pairwise Gaussian log-LR classifier over 5 pre-registered primary statistics has power >= 0.99 to separate it from M1 at a 5% false-positive rate AND the real stream lies >= 4 sd outside that model's 200-replicate distribution on at least one primary statistic. Delta-spectrum nudge bar: Bonferroni over 28 cells, alpha=0.01 two-sided, |z| >= 3.57.
entries.control_detail: Fairness device: every parameterised model bisected to the REAL lag-1 rate (0.00663836) so the doublet rate carries no discriminating information, exactly as round17/P4 did. Instrument gate: the analytic filter constant s* = 0.81288 derived from r(s)=q(1-s)/(1-q*s) reproduces lane P4's independently bisected supp = 0.8131 to 2.2e-4. Classifier power measured at 1.000 on 5 of the 6 pairs.
entries.coverage: 200 replicates per model at n = 12,956 over an archaic-English (KJV) plaintext in runes; 5 primary statistics (lag1_rate, delta_chi2_df, max_abs_delta_z, bleed28_z, abab_z); a new Delta-spectrum statistic that concentrates a single-cell rewrite signature into 28 cells instead of P4's 783-cell off-diagonal bigram table. Keystream-side and plaintext-side filtering cannot reach the observed 0.664% doublet rate at ANY suppression strength - bisection drove both to supp=0.999 and both remain 17 sd above the real rate - because a uniform other stream washes the constraint out.
not_covered: M1 (ciphertext key-skip, key desynchronises) vs M2 (ciphertext value-rewrite, key stays aligned) are ciphertext-identical by construction; measured separation power 0.175, i.e. NOT-SEPARABLE. Any sweep must cover both mechanisms because they imply different decoders.
composite loci (e.g. a filter applied to the ciphertext of an already-deduplicated plaintext)
loci that vary along the book (all models here are stationary; P4 already showed the rate is constant across the 55 pages at power 0.075, i.e. underpowered)
the 86 residual doublets are a transcription artifact until register item A-03 is run
entries.reopens_if: A high-zoom re-read (register item A-03) merges doublet neighbourhoods and moves the observed lag-1 rate; or a locus outside the seven formalised here is proposed with a distinct ciphertext prediction.
entries.notes: Settles the round10b/B4-G3 vs RECON-B/B-16 argument in B-16's favour: because the filter acts on the emitted symbol, the residual doublet rate is a property of the FILTER alone, independent of key and plaintext, so no doublet-based statistic discriminates key type in either direction.

entries.hypothesis: Rejection consumes keystream draws, so the keystream index is not the rune index. Quantify the drift, and determine which measured results in this repository depend on the alignment they assumed.
entries.threshold: The analytic mean extra-draw count must lie inside the 95% CI of 200 simulated full-book enciphers, or the drift model is wrong and everything downstream is void.
entries.control_detail: Analytic E[extra draws] = rho*(n-1) = 373.6 +/- 19.6 with rho = q*s/(1-q*s); 200 simulated enciphers of 12,956 English runes under skipdecode.encipher_keyskip at supp=0.8129 gave 374.5 +/- 21.1, 95% CI [328, 413]. Analytic inside CI.
entries.coverage: Closed form P(a rigid window of length L is drift-free) = (1-rho)^L, verified by 200 plant-and-recover trials per length at L in {25,50,100,120,200,400} with the CORRECT key and offset. Derives round17's previously unexplained prefilter survival constant: (1-rho)^PREFILTER_LEN = (1-rho)^24 = 0.495, which is pad-independent - exactly the pad-independence R17 measured (0.4-0.55 across seven pads of 4 MB to 118 MB) and attributed to 'pad statistics at least as much as size'. Closes round17 follow-up 3.
not_covered: the closed form is a LOWER bound on prefilter retention: a skip in the last one or two positions of a 24-rune window is often still survivable, which is why R17's measured mean 0.589 +/- 0.039 sits above 0.495
drift under the M2 value-rewrite locus is zero by construction; this entry quantifies drift only for the M1 key-skip locus, and A-LOCUS shows the ciphertext cannot say which is in force
entries.reopens_if: The filter locus is re-adjudicated away from ciphertext key-skip, or supp moves materially after register item A-03.
entries.notes: The practical consequence is a coverage discount, not a refutation: any rigid prefilter with a window of 50 runes or more sees a correct key less than half the time, and at 120 runes only 15% of the time.

entries.hypothesis: Every plant-and-recover control in this repository was run at <= 400 runes, yet round13/B-04 Stage D adjudicates on 12,956-rune decodes and reads a score decay as evidence that survivors were lucky. If the width-limited beam cannot hold the true path at full book length, that reading is a null from an unvalidated instrument.
entries.threshold: At L = 12,956 the beam must return score_norm >= -5.5 AND rune recovery >= 0.90, at the exact settings Stage D used (beam_w=400, max_skip=3). Fixed before the run, together with the consequence if it failed.
entries.control_detail: Planted sha256_ctr(b'CICADA3301') mod 29 - the exact B-04/G5 family - over 12,956 runes of archaic English, enciphered under skipdecode.encipher_keyskip(sign=-1, supp=0.8129). Beam at Stage-D settings returned score -4.098 with rune recovery 0.9997 and recovered the true skip count exactly (383 of 383). Wrong-key negative control at the same length: -7.305, separation 3.21.
entries.coverage: First full-book positive control in the project. Validates the skip-aware beam as an instrument at 12,956 runes, hence validates B-04 Stage D's escalation logic and any other escalation-to-full-length argument in this repo. Also delivers a fast, bit-identical re-implementation of the decoder (gate F0: 24 cases, max score delta 7.99e-15, 0 path mismatches) that cuts a full-book decode from 68 s to 7.6 s.
not_covered: this validates the DECODER at length; it says nothing about the COVERAGE of the sweep the decoder adjudicated
only the M1 key-skip cipher model was planted; a value-rewrite (M2) plant at full length is untested
beam_w values other than 400 and max_skip other than 3 were not needed because the pre-registered bar passed at Stage-D settings
plants used a single keystream family (sha256_ctr); pads with long constant byte runs are the case round17/P1 found to bind on max_skip
entries.reproduce: cd liber-primus/analysis/round18/L2-filter-leak && PYTHONUTF8=1 python3 fastbeam.py && PYTHONUTF8=1 python3 b_drawcount.py
entries.reopens_if: A pad family with long constant runs is swept at full length, where round17/P1 measured that max_skip=3 binds; or a value-rewrite plant at full length fails.
entries.notes: The worry was real and specific - the beam ranks partial paths on a raw cumulative quadgram sum over transliterations of unequal character length, which is a length-selection bias with more room to act at 12,956 runes than at 120. It does not bite: spurious skip branches desynchronise the key and lose ~1.3 per character immediately, so they die within a few positions.
